headline: High-risk cloud-workspace Devin can write shared integrations while LlamaFactory is inert; main concerns are compliance and cascading misuse, not direct bidirectional attack surface.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Devin can ingest external content via GitHub, Slack, Jira, Notion, and MCP, so prompt injection is plausible if LlamaFactory outputs are manually copied or routed through shared integrations. LlamaFactory itself has no I/O surfaces or network, so the bridge is one-way and unusual rather than default.
conditions: IF Devin is connected to a shared Slack thread, PR, or MCP server that carries LlamaFactory-generated text
IF an operator copies LlamaFactory output into Devin without review
mitigations: Disable shared integrations for the session
Require human review before pasting any LlamaFactory output into Devin
Use a fixed prompt template that strips instructions from copied text
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all cross-agent messages

B_data_leakage.rationale: Devin touches source code, issue trackers, team chat, docs, and secrets, and can write to cloud workspace files and repo clones. LlamaFactory has no filesystem or network access, so it is unlikely to exfiltrate directly, but Devin can expose sensitive data through its broad integrations and workspace outputs in default use.
conditions: IF Devin is given repositories or integrations containing secrets, tickets, or chat logs
IF Devin outputs those contents into Slack, Jira, Notion, or GitHub
mitigations: Restrict Devin to a non-sensitive repo
Remove secret-bearing files from the workspace
Turn off write access to Slack/Jira/Notion for the session
Rotate any exposed integration tokens after the run
requires-engineering: enforce data-loss-prevention filters on outbound messages

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Devin has broad write and git-modifying capabilities, while LlamaFactory has no write, shell, or network capabilities, so there is no meaningful concurrent write conflict between the pair. The only plausible conflict is indirect through shared human-managed artifacts, which is outside the default agent surfaces.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies LlamaFactory-generated edits into the same git branch Devin is modifying
mitigations: Use separate branches per agent
Avoid concurrent edits to the same files
Have Devin serialize commits through one maintainer
requires-engineering: add branch-level locking in the orchestrator

D_cascading_error.rationale: Devin is a long-running planner-executor that can act autonomously inside its workspace, so if it treats LlamaFactory output as authoritative, errors can cascade into code changes, tickets, or messages. LlamaFactory is not runnable and has no action-taking authority, but its outputs can still be misused by Devin without verification.
conditions: IF Devin consumes LlamaFactory output as facts or instructions without a verification step
IF Devin uses that output to write GitHub, Slack, Linear, Jira, or Notion
mitigations: Require Devin to cite source evidence before acting
Insert a human approval step before external writes
Limit Devin to draft-only mode
requires-engineering: add output validation against trusted sources

E_compliance.rationale: Devin handles repo deploy keys and integration tokens and can write to Slack, Linear, Jira, and Notion, creating retention and residency exposure risks if regulated data is present. LlamaFactory has no data-handling surfaces, so the compliance risk is concentrated in Devin; uncertainty about downstream storage policies warrants the higher severity.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is present in Devin's connected workspaces
IF any outbound integration retains messages or files beyond policy
mitigations: Use a workspace with no regulated data
Disable nonessential integrations
Review retention settings for Slack, Jira, and Notion
Purge session artifacts after completion
requires-engineering: document residency and retention controls per integration
